airDensity.note: Dry air at ~20 °C and sea level (1.204); 1.18 at Dallas elevation (~140 m), 1.13 at Phoenix in summer.

airDeltaTK.note: Uncontained rooms: about 20 °F (11 K) across CRAH coils; mixing and bypass air keep it low.

airDeltaTKContained.note: Containment stops bypass, so CRAH return air runs 25 to 35 °F (14 to 19 K) above supply.

distributionEfficiency.note: Busway, PDU and cabling I²R losses downstream of the UPS, typically 1 to 3%.

upsEfficiency.note: Double-conversion UPS at 40 to 80% load is 95 to 97%; eco mode reaches 99%.

transformerEfficiency.note: Medium-voltage dry-type transformers in the MVA class meet ~99% under DOE 2016 minimums at 50% load.

miscFacilityFraction.note: Lighting, office, security and BMS as a share of IT load in a large hall; small fixed loads spread over MW of IT.

crahFanFractionFallback.note: EC-fan CRAH units draw roughly 6 to 10 kW of fan power per 200 kW of sensible cooling at full speed (0.03 to 0.05).

facilityLoopDeltaTK.note: Facility-water design rise of 6 K (26/20 °C) on the reference chiller; warm-water DLC loops often run 8 to 10 K.

manifoldHeaderLossFraction.note: Flow-share drop from the first to the last rack on a direct-return row header without balancing. Headers sized so header drop is 10 to 30% of the rack branch drop give this spread; 0.2 puts an unbalanced long row in the warning band (min share ~0.89).

balancingValvePumpPenalty.note: Pressure-independent balancing valves need 15 to 30 kPa of extra head on a ~150 to 200 kPa loop, raising pump power by ~10 to 25%.

bufferAllowedRiseK.note: How far the loop may warm during a chiller restart before racks pass their coolant supply limit; 5 K keeps an 18 °C loop under typical 25 °C cold-plate limits with margin, and a 32 °C loop under 40 °C.

chillerRestartS.note: Quick-start chillers return to setpoint in under 3 minutes (York/RagingWire test); a standard restart took 13 minutes. Vendor claims range from 2 to 7 minutes to full capacity.

towerBlowdownFactor.note: Blowdown = evaporation / (cycles of concentration - 1); 4 cycles gives 0.33, 3 to 7 cycles gives 0.5 to 0.17.

peakToAverageTraining.note: Large synchronized training jobs hold GPUs near TDP; checkpoint and communication phases dip briefly, so average power sits ~85 to 95% of peak.

peakToAverageInference.note: Inference follows user demand with diurnal swings and rarely reaches TDP across a cluster (Microsoft's 2024 POLCA study found large power headroom in inference clusters); average ~50 to 75% of peak.

dacReachM.note: Passive 800G copper at 100G per lane reaches 2 to 3 m; reseller listings give 2 m maximum, and 200G-per-lane links shorten it further.

aecReachM.note: 800G active electrical cables with retimers are listed up to 7 m across vendors.

fiberNsPerM.note: Group index ~1.47 in silica fibre: 1.47 / 0.2998 m/ns.

copperNsPerM.note: Twinax velocity factor ~0.7 to 0.8 of c.

hopNs.note: Port-to-port latency of a 51.2T Ethernet AI switch is ~0.5 to 0.8 µs; InfiniBand switches are ~0.15 to 0.25 µs.

pipingUsdPerMRaised.note: Installed supply and return pair of DN80 to DN150 stainless or PP-R under a raised floor, including insulation and leak detection.

pipingUsdPerMOverhead.note: Same pipe overhead plus hangers, seismic bracing and drip trays; roughly a third more than under-floor.

raisedFloorInstallWeeks.note: Under-floor runs are easy to route but must be coordinated with pedestals and cable trays per hall.

overheadInstallWeeks.note: Overhead adds structural supports and drip trays before pipe can be hung.

routingSlackM.note: Per run: vertical drops, bends and service loops beyond the straight-line distance.

warnThreshold.note: Utilization above 80% of a capacity is flagged as a warning, a common engineering design margin.

sources.title: Engineering ToolBox: propylene glycol based heat-transfer fluids

entries.summary: Water with 40% propylene glycol for outdoor loops in cold climates (freeze point about -22 °C). Carries about 10% less heat per kilogram than PG25 and is twice as viscous, so it needs more pump power.

densityKgM3.note: 1030 kg/m³ at 20 °C, 1016 at 40 °C; specific gravity 1.034 at 60 °F.

viscosityPaS.note: About 4.5 mPa·s at 20 °C for 40% PG (ASHRAE Fundamentals glycol tables); roughly 3 mPa·s at 35 °C.

cpJPerKgK.note: Liquid cp 0.298 Btu/lb°F at 30 °C per Honeywell's Solstice zd data (page did not load during research; value from search excerpt). Sensible cp is secondary; two-phase heat transport uses latent heat (~190 kJ/kg).

densityKgM3.note: Liquid at the 18.3 °C normal boiling point (Honeywell data via search excerpt); ~1250 at 30 °C.

entries.name: Adiabatic dry cooler

sources.title: TechTarget on Schneider Electric 32 C vs 45 C TCS modeling in Dallas and Paris

entries.summary: A dry cooler with wetted pads or sprays that pre-cool the inlet air toward wet-bulb on hot hours. Runs dry most of the year and spends water only when it is hot, which avoids most trim-chiller hours.

approachK.note: Same coil approach as the dry cooler; in adiabatic mode the engine applies it to wet-bulb. Real pads reach 80 to 90% saturation, so the true air temperature is 1 to 2 K above wet-bulb in Dallas summer, which this slightly flatters.

fanPowerFraction.note: Same fan class as a dry cooler.

waterLPerKwh.note: Only during adiabatic hours. Air through the coil per kWh at ~10 K air rise is 3600 / (1.006 x 10) = 360 kg; pre-cooling it 7 to 10 K evaporates 360 x 1.006 x 8 / 2450 = 1.2 kg. Minus pad efficiency gains, plus bleed. Schneider's Paris model averaged 0.07 L/kWh over a year because adiabatic hours are few.

adiabaticAboveC.note: Set where the dry coil alone stops meeting a 32 °C supply (32 - 7 K approach); vendors default to switch-on points of about 22 to 28 °C.

unitCapacityW.note: Same unit sizes as dry coolers with a wetted-pad kit.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Dry cooler plus pads, water treatment and controls, about a third more per kW.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Dry cooler lead time plus water-treatment skid.

installWeeks.note: Dry cooler install plus water supply, drain and treatment.

footprintM2PerMw.note: Pre-cooling lets a smaller coil hit the same summer design point than a pure dry cooler (60 m²/MW).

entries.name: Air-cooled chiller with free cooling

sources.title: Vertiv Liebert AFC free-cooling chiller data sheet

entries.summary: Screw compressors make cold water at any outdoor temperature, with a free-cooling coil that takes over when it is cold outside. Works for air-cooled halls at 18 to 20 °C supply, but compressor power climbs as the outdoor temperature rises.

approachK.note: Fitted to the vendor's free-cooling zero-energy temperature (ZET): 9.1 to 11.0 °C at 20/26 °C water. With the engine's rule (T_out + approach <= supply - loop ΔT, ΔT = 6 K) that is a 3 to 5 K approach.

copRef.note: Nominal EER 4.2 to 4.55 at 35 °C air, 20 °C supply / 26 °C return (R1234ze and R134a screw models, 0.7 to 1.5 MW).

copRefOutdoorC.note: Rating condition of the EER above.

copSlopePerK.note: COP falls ~2.5 to 3% per K of extra condenser lift (Carnot lift ratio around a 15 °C evaporator and a 47 °C condenser, discounted for fixed losses). Gives COP ~6 at 20 °C outdoor and ~3 at 45 °C, inside the 4 to 7 anchor band for normal hours.

fanPowerFraction.note: EC condenser fans in free-cooling mode; roughly a tenth of compressor-mode input power at nominal capacity (1/4.3 = 0.23 W/W).

waterLPerKwh.note: Closed loop, air-cooled condenser: no evaporation.

unitCapacityW.note: Range 650 to 1,500 kW; 1,296 kW (CIZ125) chosen as the reference unit.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Air-cooled free-cooling chiller equipment at roughly 900 to 1,400 USD per ton (250 to 400 USD/kW) plus pumps, piping and controls. Market guides quote 1,000 to 2,100 USD per ton equipment for smaller units; MW-scale units are cheaper per kW.

leadTimeWeeks.note: 2025-26 supplier tables put large chillers at 20 to 85 weeks against ~40 weeks before 2020 (recruiter-compiled; not primary).

installWeeks.note: Crane set, piping, electrical and commissioning per plant.

footprintM2PerMw.note: CIZ125 is 10.835 x 2.35 m for 1,296 kW = 19.7 m²/MW bare; airflow clearance and service access roughly double it.

entries.name: Evaporative cooling tower

sources.title: Delta Cooling Towers: how to calculate water loss in a cooling tower

entries.summary: Water is sprayed through fill while fans pull air across it; evaporation cools the rest of the water to a few kelvin above wet-bulb. The most compact and efficient heat rejection, but it evaporates about 1.5 L per kWh plus blowdown.

approachK.note: Approach to wet-bulb; ~4 K is the nominal design for large data-center towers (ASHRAE practice), 2.5 K possible with oversized fill. Excludes an isolating plate heat exchanger (another 1 to 2 K).

fanPowerFraction.note: Induced-draft tower fans run about 0.03 to 0.09 kW per ton of heat rejected (0.008 to 0.025 W/W).

waterLPerKwh.note: Evaporation: 3.6 MJ per kWh / 2.43 MJ/kg latent heat at ~30 °C = 1.48 kg. Some heat leaves as sensible air heating (lower), while drift adds 0.001 to 0.2% of circulation (higher). Blowdown is added with towerBlowdownFactor.

unitCapacityW.note: Typical factory-assembled or field-erected cell size for data-center plants.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Tower cells, plate heat exchanger and water treatment; cheapest per kW of the four because evaporation shrinks the equipment.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Modular factory-built cells are faster than chillers; no primary 2025 figure found.

installWeeks.note: Basin, piping, water treatment and controls.

footprintM2PerMw.note: Evaporative towers reject several times more heat per square metre than dry coils.

entries.name: Dry cooler

sources.title: TechTarget on Schneider Electric 32 C vs 45 C TCS modeling in Dallas and Paris

entries.summary: Fans blow outdoor air over a finned coil; the water can only get to a few kelvin above the outdoor dry-bulb temperature. Uses no water and little power, so it pairs with warm-water liquid cooling. On hot hours it needs a trim chiller.

approachK.note: Schneider's 100 MW model (Dallas, Paris) starts chiller assist at ~25 °C outdoor for a 32 °C supply and ~35 °C for 45 °C supply: approach of 7 to 10 K. Larger coils reach 5 K at higher capex.

copRef.note: No compressor; trim cooling uses the chiller entry's curve.

fanPowerFraction.note: EC-fan V-coil dry coolers at design duty draw roughly 15 to 30 kW of fan power per MW rejected; less at part load.

waterLPerKwh.note: Sealed closed loop, sensible heat only.

unitCapacityW.note: Data-center V-coil dry coolers are sold from 150 kW to 1.8 MW (LU-VE) and up to 2.5 MW (ENEX); 1 MW is a typical unit at warm-water conditions.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Coil-and-fan equipment without compressors; cheaper per unit than a chiller but large coil area for small approach. No primary cost source found.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Shorter than chillers (no compressors) but caught in the same 2025-26 cooling backlog that Linesight flagged.

installWeeks.note: Roof or yard set, piping and controls.

footprintM2PerMw.note: A 1 MW V-coil unit is roughly 12 x 2.3 m; 7 K approach needs more coil per MW than a chiller condenser, plus spacing to avoid hot-air recirculation.

entries.name: Air with hot- or cold-aisle containment

sources.title: Uptime Institute Cooling Systems Survey 2024

entries.summary: Server fans push room air through the rack; CRAH coils on the facility loop take the heat. Containment keeps hot and cold air apart, which raises the usable air temperature rise and the practical rack limit to roughly 30 to 40 kW.

maxRackW.note: Uptime 2024 survey (n=820): most operators put the point where air becomes too costly between 20 and 39 kW per rack (29% at 20-29 kW, 19% at 30-39 kW). 40 kW is the upper end with good containment; secondary press cites ~50 kW as the absolute ceiling.

toTechnicalLoop.note: No liquid at the rack; all heat leaves as air to CRAH units.

min.note: Classic chilled-water supply to CRAH coils.

max.note: ASHRAE recommended server inlet air tops out at 27 °C; a CRAH coil needs about 3 K approach, so chilled water above ~24 °C cannot hold the cold aisle in range.

deltaTK.note: Air temperature rise across the rack with containment; matches the rules value airDeltaTKContained.

pressureDropKpa.note: No liquid circuit at the rack; the coil pressure drop belongs to the CRAH.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Containment panels, blanking and doors spread per rack (aluminium/polycarbonate panels are a few kg per 600 mm bay).

pumpPowerFraction.note: No pump at the rack; CRAH fan power is counted on the CRAH equipment (or crahFanFractionFallback).

capexUsdPerKw.note: Containment hardware only (aisle doors, roof panels, blanking), about 1,500 to 3,000 USD per rack bay spread over 20 to 40 kW. CRAH units and the chiller plant are costed separately.

installWeeks.note: Containment kits are bolted onto existing rows; a hall is typically done in days to a few weeks.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Containment is a commodity sheet-metal product with short manufacturing lead times.

entries.name: Direct-to-chip, single-phase

sources.title: Lenovo GB300 NVL72 3D tour (18 kW air / 118 kW liquid)
Upsite: ASHRAE 5th edition liquid cooling classes W17 to W+
Vertiv and NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 7 MW reference architecture (132 kW per rack)
Introl: direct-to-chip cooling implementation (capex, CDU pressures)

entries.summary: Cold plates on GPUs, CPUs and switches carry about 85% of rack heat into a PG25 technical loop fed by a CDU. Works with warm facility water up to 45 °C, which lets dry coolers do most of the heat rejection. The remaining ~15% still needs air.

maxRackW.note: Shipping DLC racks run 132 to 140 kW (GB300 NVL72); Vera Rubin NVL72 class racks are 190 to 230 kW and NVIDIA's 600 kW Kyber roadmap is still single-phase cold plate. 250 kW is set as the practical rack-manifold limit today.

toTechnicalLoop.note: Lenovo GB300 NVL72: 118 kW liquid, 18 kW air (0.87); 85% of the rack is liquid cooled, 90% of compute trays.

min.note: ASHRAE W17 class upper bound; colder facility water adds condensation risk without benefit.

max.note: ASHRAE W45 class upper limit; NVIDIA rates Vera Rubin for 45 °C inlet water.

deltaTK.note: Technical-loop temperature rise. Published flow figures for NVL72 range from ~1.0 to 1.5 L/min per kW, which with PG25 is a 10 to 15 K rise; 10 K is the common design point.

pressureDropKpa.note: Rack manifold plus cold plates and quick disconnects; secondary reporting cites NVIDIA's GB200 limit as 1.5 bar. CDU pumps deliver 350 to 500 kPa differential (Introl).

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Rack manifolds, hoses and ~30 to 40 L of coolant in the rack and branch lines; cold plates are already in the rack's own weight.

pumpPowerFraction.note: CDU pump power per unit of liquid heat. Pumping 0.1 L/s per 10 kW at ~300 kPa with 60% pump efficiency is 0.5 kW per 100 kW; real CDUs run 1 to 2% with controls and margin. Use this or the CDU entry's pumpPowerW, not both.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Rack-level only: in-rack manifolds, hoses and quick disconnects at about 5,000 to 15,000 USD per rack (secondary press) over a 132 kW rack. CDUs, piping and heat rejection are costed separately. Whole-system DLC capex is quoted at 1,500 to 3,000 USD/kW (Introl).

installWeeks.note: Row manifolds, flushing, pressure testing and commissioning of the technical loop.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Manifolds and quick disconnects follow GPU rack allocation; 2025-26 DLC parts ran four to seven months.

entries.name: Direct-to-chip, two-phase

sources.title: Converge Digest: Accelsius MR250 two-phase CDU (250 kW per rack, 45 C facility water)

entries.summary: A low-pressure refrigerant boils inside the cold plates, taking heat at nearly constant temperature. Handles higher heat flux per chip than water cold plates. Shipping as row CDUs of about 250 kW per rack, but the installed base is small.

maxRackW.note: Accelsius MR250: 250 kW per rack, or two 125 kW racks.

toTechnicalLoop.note: Same cold-plate coverage as single-phase DLC; the rack still sheds drives, optics and PSU heat to air.

min.note: Accelsius 2025 full-rack test ran PG25 facility water at 20, 30 and 40 °C.

max.note: MR250 supports facility water up to 45 °C.

deltaTK.note: Facility-side water rise across the two-phase CDU. Accelsius' test fed 375 L/min PG25 for 250 kW: 250 kW / (6.25 L/s x 1.02 kg/L x 3.95 kJ/kgK) = 9.9 K. The refrigerant side boils near-isothermally, so sensible flow sizing does not apply to it.

pressureDropKpa.note: Refrigerant loops run at low mass flow (latent heat ~190 kJ/kg vs ~40 kJ/kg sensible for 10 K of water), so drops are lower than single-phase loops.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Manifolds and refrigerant charge; refrigerant inventory is smaller than a water loop for the same heat.

pumpPowerFraction.note: Mass flow is Q / h_fg = 250 kW / 190 kJ/kg = 1.3 kg/s; at ~100 kPa head this is well under 1 kW. Doubled for controls and margin.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Rack-level manifolds, cold plates and refrigerant charge priced at about 1.5x single-phase hardware because of low volume and pressure-rated parts.

installWeeks.note: Refrigerant handling, leak testing and charge add work beyond a water loop.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Few suppliers; Accelsius cites a 500% manufacturing expansion, which suggests constrained supply.

entries.name: Single-phase immersion tank

sources.title: Submer SmartPod EVO800 data sheet Rev.01 (hosted by OCP)

entries.summary: Servers sit vertically in a tank of dielectric oil that in-tank CDUs cool with facility water. Almost all heat goes to the fluid. Tanks are heavy (about 1.8 t filled) and need hardware qualified for immersion.

maxRackW.note: EVO800: up to 100 kW at 26 °C water inlet and 50 °C setpoint (50 kW fully redundant); 140 kW at 22 °C water and 55 °C setpoint.

toTechnicalLoop.note: Thermal loss to the room is 550 W with a closed lid at 55 °C setpoint, about 0.5% of 100 kW.

deltaTK.note: Expected 5 K water outlet increase at rated flow.

pressureDropKpa.note: Water head loss per in-tank CDU: 40 kPa at 5 m³/h, 130 kPa at 9 m³/h.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Pod plus SmartCoolant, before IT hardware (empty pod 800 kg, 1,187 L fluid). Max floor load 19 kN/m² with IT.

tankFootprintM2PerRack.note: Tank footprint 2.28 x 0.97 m; one tank holds 39 OU, about one rack. Operational footprint with service space is 7.4 m² per tank in a deployment.

pumpPowerFraction.note: Power consumption per kW IT: 0.016 at 50 kW, 0.011 at 70 kW (two in-tank CDUs, 1.6 kW nominal).

capexUsdPerKw.note: Tank with in-tank CDUs at roughly 50,000 to 80,000 USD plus ~1,200 L of synthetic fluid at 20 to 40 USD/L, over ~100 kW.

installWeeks.note: Floor reinforcement checks, tank placement, fluid fill and IT integration.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Built-to-order tanks plus immersion-qualified servers.

entries.name: Two-phase immersion tank

sources.title: 3M Novec 649 Engineered Fluid technical data

entries.summary: Servers sit in a fluorocarbon bath that boils on the chips and condenses on a water coil in the lid. Very high density, but the fluids are PFAS and 3M stopped making Novec and Fluorinert at the end of 2025, so new projects have stalled.

maxRackW.note: LiquidStack markets its 48U DataTank at up to 252 kW (vendor listing seen in search, not opened).

toTechnicalLoop.note: Vapor condenses on the in-tank coil; small losses through the lid and when the tank is opened.

min.note: Condenser water must stay well below the fluid's boiling point (49 °C for Novec 649).

max.note: Above ~40 °C the condenser cannot hold vapor pressure with a 49 to 61 °C boiling fluid.

deltaTK.note: Condenser water rise; the bath itself is isothermal at the boiling point.

pressureDropKpa.note: Condenser coil water-side drop, similar to single-phase tank CDUs.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Fluorocarbons are ~1.6 kg/L (Novec 649), about double a hydrocarbon oil, so a filled tank outweighs a single-phase tank.

tankFootprintM2PerRack.note: 48U tank; no published footprint found. Assumed slightly larger than a 39 OU single-phase tank (2.22 m²).

pumpPowerFraction.note: No fluid pump in the bath (passive boiling); condenser water pump only.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Sealed tank plus fluorocarbon fill at several times hydrocarbon-oil prices per litre, and fluid now scarce.

installWeeks.note: Sealed tanks, vapor management and fluid handling.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Fluid supply is the constraint after 3M's PFAS exit; replacements (e.g. Chemours Opteon 2P50) are not yet at scale.

entries.name: Active rear-door heat exchanger

sources.title: Supermicro Rear Door Heat Exchanger (RDHx) data sheet

entries.summary: A rear-door water coil with its own EC fans, so it can pull more air than the servers alone and cool roughly 50 to 75 kW per rack, with 120 kW models now listed. Fans add about 3% parasitic power.

maxRackW.note: Supermicro lists active doors at 50, 80, 100 and 120 kW; Motivair ChilledDoor is marketed up to 75 kW. 75 kW is the common mid-range rating.

toTechnicalLoop.note: On facility water (or a dedicated loop), not a CDU technical loop.

toFacilityWaterAtRack.note: Vendor positions the door to remove all residual rack heat.

min.note: Kept above room dew point to avoid condensation; vendors include anti-condensation control.

max.note: Active fans let the door work with warmer water than a passive door, but rated duties assume about 18 °C (65 °F) water; capacity derates sharply toward 24 °C.

deltaTK.note: Typical water rise on active doors; no duty table was available in the Supermicro sheet.

pressureDropKpa.note: Larger coils at higher flow than the passive door (30 kPa at max duty), so higher drop.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Supermicro active doors weigh 114 to 160 kg without coolant; a few litres of water add ~5 kg.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Active doors are roughly 15,000 to 30,000 USD installed; divided by 50 to 75 kW.

installWeeks.note: Door mounting plus power and water hook-up per row.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Demand from AI retrofits has stretched active RDHx lead times beyond passive doors.

entries.name: Passive rear-door heat exchanger

sources.title: USystems ColdLogik CL21 Smart Passive RDHx data sheet

entries.summary: A water coil replaces the rack's rear door and the server fans push hot exhaust through it. No fans of its own, so capacity depends on server airflow and needs cool water, roughly 20 to 30 kW per rack.

maxRackW.note: CL21 Smart Passive with 14 °C water in / 20 °C out at 6,000 m³/h server airflow: 22 kW at 35 °C air-on, 29 kW at 40 °C air-on. Vertiv markets its passive Liebert DCD up to 50 kW but no duty table was found.

toTechnicalLoop.note: The door sits on facility water directly; nothing goes to a CDU technical loop.

toFacilityWaterAtRack.note: Sized to neutralize the rack's exhaust; real capture falls below 1.0 when server airflow or water temperature is outside the duty table.

min.note: Rated duty is at 14 °C water in; colder water risks condensation on the door.

max.note: Passive doors lose capacity fast as water warms because the server exhaust temperature fixes the air side; above ~20 °C the door cannot cool to room-neutral.

pressureDropKpa.note: Fluid pressure drop at max duty (6,000 m³/h, 40 °C air-on); 2.3 kPa at the smallest duty point.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Wet weight including interface frame, 750 mm wide 42U door; 600 mm 42U is 88 kg and 800 mm 52U is 125 kg.

pumpPowerFraction.note: No fans or pumps in the door ('zero operational costs'); server fans and the facility pump do the work.

capexUsdPerKw.note: A passive door costs roughly 6,000 to 15,000 USD installed with hoses; divided by about 25 kW.

installWeeks.note: Door swap plus flexible hoses to under-floor or overhead branch piping, per row.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Built-to-order coils; typical quoted lead times for RDHx are two to four months.

entries.name: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72

sources.title: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 product page
Lenovo GB300 NVL72 mechanical specifications
Lenovo GB300 NVL72 environmental specifications
Lenovo GB300 NVL72 technical specifications
ModulEdge: GB300 NVL72, what one rack demands
Data Gravity: How much does an NVIDIA NVL72 cost?
PC Games Hardware: Vera Rubin NVL72 rack price (Morgan Stanley estimate)

entries.summary: 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs in one 48U MGX rack: 18 compute trays, 9 NVLink switch trays, 8 power shelves feeding a 50 to 54 V DC busbar. About 85 to 90% of the heat goes to liquid; the rest needs air.

nominalPowerW.note: HPE QuickSpecs (a50009244enw) give 132 kW nominal TDP; the hpe.com page timed out, so ModulEdge's restatement is cited. ModulEdge's own planning figure is up to 142 kW.

peakPowerW.note: EDPp about 155 kW per HPE QuickSpecs, as restated by ModulEdge. HPE advises provisioning busway for 192 kW.

weightKg.note: Approximately 1,580 kg, depending on the configuration.

depthMm.note: 1,068 mm rack, expanding to 1,200 mm with the extension frame. The footprint uses 1,200 mm.

maxLiquidFraction.note: ModulEdge reports Lenovo's split as roughly 90% liquid, 10% air. Integrators commonly quote 85 to 90%; the low end is used so the air side is not undersized.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: ASHRAE W45. Lenovo lists operating water at 2 to 50 °C but publishes flow and pressure drop only up to 45 °C supply (177 L/min, 18.4 psi).

fp8Pflops.note: Dense. NVIDIA lists 720 PFLOPS FP8 with sparsity per rack; dense is half.

capexUsd.note: No list price. Data Gravity reports small-order POs just under $5.0M without an in-rack CDU; Morgan Stanley's bill-of-materials estimate (via PC Games Hardware) is about $4M for hyperscalers. Midpoint used.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Shipping product, but allocation-constrained. Assumed 12 to 26 weeks from PO to delivery, depending on buyer volume and ODM.

entries.name: AMD Helios

sources.title: Supermicro AMD Helios platform datasheet
remio: AMD Helios unites 72 GPUs (power load)
TechCrunch: AMD's Helios rack weighs the same as two compact cars
ABI Research: AMD and Schneider Electric Helios reference design
OCP Marketplace: Rittal Open Rack Wide (ORW)
ai2.work: Inside AMD's $5.25M Helios rack

entries.summary: 72 MI455X GPUs and 18 EPYC Venice CPUs in a double-wide OCP Open Rack Wide (1,200 mm) frame with UALink over Ethernet scale-up. Weight reports conflict (about 5,000 vs about 7,000 lb); the heavier figure is used. Switch and power tray counts are estimates.

nominalPowerW.note: Reporting from AMD's Advancing AI event puts the rack load at 225 to 245 kW. One outlet (ai2.work) gives about 140 kW, which conflicts with every other source and is ignored.

peakPowerW.note: AMD and Schneider Electric reference design supports racks up to 246 kW. This is a planning envelope, not a per-SKU rating.

weightKg.note: Reports conflict. Lisa Su: nearly 7,000 lb (3,175 kg). remio cites published platform details at about 5,000 lb (2,268 kg). The heavier figure is used so floor checks stay conservative.

widthMm.note: Open Rack Wide enclosure dimensions (Rittal ORW listing, 4,700 kg tested payload). A Helios-specific drawing is not public.

heightMm.note: Open Rack Wide enclosure height (Meta's ORW design spec lists 2,390 mm).

maxLiquidFraction.note: AMD and Schneider reference design removes up to 84% of heat through liquid cooling.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: Not published; AMD only says high allowable coolant temperature. ASHRAE W40 assumed, 5 K below NVIDIA's 45 °C Vera Rubin inlet.

fp8Pflops.note: FP8 1.4 exaFLOPS per rack. Sparsity is not stated.

capexUsd.note: No list price. Analysts (Futurum's Daniel Newman) put it at $5M to $5.5M per rack; midpoint used.

leadTimeWeeks.note: In production since July 2026, initial shipments at the end of Q3 and a broader ramp through Q4 2026. Assumed 20 to 36 weeks for orders placed now.

entries.name: HGX B300 air-cooled rack (2 servers)

sources.title: NVIDIA DGX B300 product page
NVIDIA HGX platform page (HGX B300 specs)
Supermicro SYS-822GS-NB3RT (HGX B300, 8U air) product page
Supermicro NVIDIA accelerated systems page

entries.summary: Standard air-cooled rack holding two 8-GPU HGX B300 servers (16 GPUs), the usual density in halls without liquid. About 14 kW per server. Power is AC to server PSUs, which this app groups with the 54 V AC chain.

nominalPowerW.note: 2 servers x about 14 kW (NVIDIA DGX B300 system power usage).

peakPowerW.note: 2 servers at about 14.5 kW each plus about 1 kW for the management switch, PDUs and fans at full speed. Bounded above by PSU capacity: Supermicro's 3+3 x 6.6 kW PSUs give 19.8 kW per server.

weightKg.note: 2 x 119 kg (Supermicro SYS-822GS-NB3RT net weight) + about 140 kg empty 42U enclosure + about 60 kg PDUs, switch and cabling.

widthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

depthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor. The 950 mm deep server chassis needs at least 1,100 mm.

heightMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Air-cooled system with no cold plates: all heat goes to air. A rear-door heat exchanger moves it to water at the rack.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: Not applicable: air-cooled servers have no liquid loop. Facility water limits come from the RDHx or air handler serving the rack.

fp8Pflops.note: Dense. 2 servers x 36 PFLOPS FP8 dense per HGX B300 (72 sparse / 2).

capexUsd.note: No public list price. Scaled from GB300 NVL72 at about $4M to $5M per 72 GPUs (about $55k to $70k per GPU all-in): 16 GPUs at about $55k to $65k, plus about $30k for enclosure, PDUs and management switch.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Shipping volume product from many OEMs (NVIDIA: HGX B300 shipping now). Assumed 8 to 16 weeks from order to delivery for a standard configuration.

entries.name: AMD MI355X air-cooled rack (2 servers)

sources.title: Supermicro AS-A126GS-TNMR (MI355X, 10U air) product page
Glenn Lockwood: MI355X notes (quotes the AMD MI355X brochure)

entries.summary: Standard air-cooled rack holding two 10U 8-GPU MI355X servers (16 GPUs), such as Supermicro's AS-A126GS-TNMR. Rack power is an estimate built from the GPU board power. Power is AC to server PSUs.

nominalPowerW.note: Per server: 8 x 1,400 W GPUs = 11.2 kW, 2 CPUs at up to 500 W = 1 kW, 19 heavy-duty fans about 1 kW at typical load, memory, NICs and drives about 0.8 kW, giving about 14 kW. Two servers.

peakPowerW.note: Nominal plus fans at full speed and GPU transients, about 15.5 kW per server. Bounded above by 4 x 6.6 kW active PSUs = 26.4 kW per server.

weightKg.note: 2 x 133 kg (Supermicro AS-A126GS-TNMR net weight) + about 140 kg empty 42U enclosure + about 60 kg PDUs, switch and cabling.

widthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

depthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor. The server chassis is 843 mm deep.

heightMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Air-cooled OAM modules with no cold plates: all heat goes to air. A rear-door heat exchanger moves it to water at the rack.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: Not applicable: air-cooled servers have no liquid loop. Facility water limits come from the RDHx or air handler serving the rack.

capexUsd.note: No public price. Assumed about $25k to $30k per MI355X GPU plus about $60k to $80k per server for chassis, CPUs, memory and NICs, plus about $30k for enclosure and PDUs.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Shipping since the second half of 2025 from several OEMs. Assumed 8 to 16 weeks for a standard configuration.

entries.name: Network rack (8 x 64-port 800G switches)

sources.title: NVIDIA Spectrum-4 SN5000 2U switch hardware specifications

entries.summary: Air-cooled rack for leaf and spine switches: eight 2U 64-port 800G switches (Spectrum-4 SN5600 class) with patch panels. Power excludes pluggable optics, which the engine counts separately. Power and weight can be overridden per placement.

nominalPowerW.note: 8 switches x 940 W typical power with passive cables (SN5600). Excludes optics.

peakPowerW.note: About 1.5 kW per switch at full traffic and fan speed, 8 switches. Each switch is bounded by its 3 kW PSUs (1+1). Excludes optics.

weightKg.note: 8 x 23.5 kg switches = 188 kg + about 140 kg empty 42U enclosure + about 170 kg patch panels, cable managers and fiber/copper bundles.

widthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

depthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

heightMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Fan-cooled switches with no cold plates: all heat goes to air.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: Not applicable: air-cooled switches have no liquid loop.

capexUsd.note: Assumed about $70k per 64-port 800G switch with software license x 8, plus about $40k for enclosure, PDUs and patch panels. Excludes optics.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Assumed 8 to 20 weeks for 800G switches; supply has tracked GPU demand.

entries.name: Storage rack (all-flash NVMe)
entries.summary: Air-cooled rack of all-flash NVMe storage nodes serving training data and checkpoints. Generic sizing: 16 x 2U nodes, each with two 400G ports. Power and weight can be overridden per placement.

nominalPowerW.note: 16 x 2U all-flash nodes at about 750 W each under load.

peakPowerW.note: Nominal plus about 25% for rebuilds, write bursts and fan ramp.

weightKg.note: 16 nodes x about 30 kg = 480 kg + about 140 kg empty enclosure + about 80 kg PDUs, switch and cabling.

widthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

depthMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

heightMm.note: Generic 42U enclosure, 600 mm wide by 1,200 mm deep by 2,000 mm tall; actual size depends on the enclosure vendor.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Fan-cooled storage nodes with no cold plates: all heat goes to air.

maxCoolantSupplyC.note: Not applicable: air-cooled storage has no liquid loop.

capexUsd.note: Assumed about $45k to $55k per all-flash node with drives, x 16, plus enclosure and PDUs. Varies widely with capacity and vendor.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Assumed 6 to 12 weeks for standard all-flash storage nodes.

entries.name: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72

sources.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 product page
NVIDIA DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 user guide: hardware
Cisco AI Rack for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 data sheet
Civo: Vera Rubin NVL72 rack details
ModulEdge: NVIDIA Vera Rubin for data center providers
PC Games Hardware: Vera Rubin NVL72 rack price (Morgan Stanley estimate)

entries.summary: 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs on the third-generation MGX rack: 18 fanless compute trays, 9 NVLink 6 switch trays, 4 x 110 kW power shelves, 45 °C inlet water. Early access since September 2026; power, weight and price are estimates.

nominalPowerW.note: NVIDIA has not published rack power. ModulEdge puts VR200 NVL72 at roughly 190 to 230 kW; midpoint used.

peakPowerW.note: Gigabyte's VR NVL72 POD page lists rack power up to 240 kW (seen in search results; the page returned 403 when fetched). Consistent with 4 x 110 kW shelves run redundant (220 kW per side) plus headroom.

weightKg.note: Not published. Started from GB300 NVL72 at 1,580 kg, added the deeper and taller rack (1,200 x 2,300 mm vs 1,068 x 2,236 mm), the liquid-cooled busbar and about twice the coolant flow, and took out the tray fans. About +15%.

widthMm.note: Civo rack spec table: 600 x 1,200 x 2,300 mm.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Compute and switch trays are fully liquid cooled (Civo: 100% direct liquid), but NVIDIA's guide says the power shelves use air-cooled PSUs. About 2 to 3% PSU loss plus the two management switches go to air.

capexUsd.note: Morgan Stanley bill-of-materials estimate of about $7.8M per rack for hyperscalers (via PC Games Hardware). Later analyst figures driven by HBM4 prices run to about $9.1M.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Early access since September 2026, volume ramp in the second half of 2026 (ModulEdge); Cisco says availability dates are to be announced. Assumed 26 to 40 weeks for orders placed now.
